gingival zenith positions are significantly different in the maxillary central and lateral incisors, and that gingival zenith position is significantly correlated to the level of the incisal edges.

the gingival zenith position and levels of maxillary anterior dentitions are not related to the tooth size, but the gingival zenith positions and the levels of maxillary central and lateral incisors are significantly related to the tooth shape.

the relationship between the position of the gingival zenith and the level of the maxillary central incisor.
the gingival zenith positions of the maxillary incisors and canines, and the gingival zenith levels of the maxillay incisors and canins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gingival zeniths are located on the middle third of the facial surfaces of teeth.
gingival zeniths are not a reliable and valid indicator for the position of the maxillary dentition.
the maxillary anterior gingival zeniths of the central incisors and lateral incisors are positioned at a level that is approximately 1.5 mm below the CEJ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

gingival zeniths are positioned in relation to the incisal edges of the maxillary central incisors and that the levels of the gingival zeniths of the maxillary lateral incisors are positioned at the level of the gingival margins of the central incisors.
the gingival zenith positions and gingival zenith levels of the maxilla anterior dentition are not constant and are influenced by the position of the tooth, tooth size, tooth shape, and gender.
the gingival zenith position of the maxillary incisors, canines and premolars is not influenced by tooth size, gender, ethnicity or tooth shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gingival zenith position and the level of the anterior maxillary dentition are not related.
the gingival zenith position is a reliable landmark for the determination of the maxillary incisal edge position in the maxillary incisors.
gingival zenith positions and the level of the maxillary incisors can be used to predict the level of the gingival zenith in the contralateral tooth, as well as the level of the incisal edges.
